record.paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
record.context_brief: Global stability for the constant-population SAIRS model beyond beta_e<gamma
record.original_question: For the eight-parameter constant-population SAIRS model obtained by setting the disease-induced death rate delta to zero, with vaccination, loss of immunity, exposed/asymptomatic transmission beta_e, and infective transmission beta_i, can global stability of the unique endemic equilibrium be proved beyond the currently resolved case beta_e<gamma?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following SAIRS-with-vaccination compartmental epidemic model on a constant total population (normalized to 1), with compartments S (susceptible), A (exposed/asymptomatic infectious), I (symptomatic infectious), R (recovered/immune). With nonnegative parameters Λ (birth rate equal to natural death rate μ so the population is constant), β_e (transmission rate from asymptomatic), β_i (transmission rate from symptomatic), α (rate of progression A→I), γ (recovery rate from I), γ_A (recovery rate from A), ν (vaccination rate S→R), and ρ (loss-of-immunity rate R→S), the dynamics are

   dS/dt = Λ − (β_e A + β_i I) S − (μ + ν) S + ρ R,
   dA/dt = (β_e A + β_i I) S − (α + γ_A + μ) A,
   dI/dt = α A − (γ + μ) I,
   dR/dt = γ_A A + γ I + ν S − (μ + ρ) R,

with S + A + I + R = 1.

Define the basic reproduction number R_0 in the usual next-generation way. Assume R_0 > 1 so that a unique endemic equilibrium E* with all coordinates positive exists in the simplex.

Problem. Prove that the endemic equilibrium E* is globally asymptotically stable in the positively invariant region {(S,A,I,R) : S,A,I,R ≥ 0, S+A+I+R = 1, (A,I) ≠ (0,0)} whenever R_0 > 1, without the additional restriction β_e < γ (under which restriction global asymptotic stability is already known). Equivalently, remove the parameter restriction β_e < γ from the known global stability result.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that the endemic equilibrium of the SAIRS model with vaccination is globally asymptotically stable whenever R_0 > 1 without additional parameter restrictions appears to remain open. Recent works (Ottaviano–Sensi–Sottile 2021/2022 and the multi-group extension 2022/2023) explicitly state that they can only establish global stability under restrictions such as β_e < γ (or equal recovery rates for A and I), and numerical simulations suggest the unrestricted statement holds but has not been proved.

status_evidence.title: Global stability of SAIRS epidemic models (arXiv:2109.05122)
status_evidence.snippet: Global stability of the endemic equilibrium is proven only under additional restrictions; the unrestricted case is conjectured based on numerical evidence.
status_evidence.claim: Global asymptotic stability of the SAIRS endemic equilibrium is established only under parameter restrictions; the general case remains conjectural.

status_evidence.title: Global stability of multi-group SAIRS epidemic models (arXiv:2202.02993)
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient conditions are obtained under restrictions on recovery rates; the unrestricted endemic global stability remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The multi-group extension still requires extra restrictions, indicating the original conjecture is unresolved.
